title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2610.34514v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Estimating neural scaling laws involves an end-to-end pipeline: designing a scaling recipe, training models across scales, evaluating models on a target metric, and deploying an algorithm to fit a scaling law to the resulting data. This final fitting stage is often treated as routine: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss using local optimization from a grid of initializations, and return the best solution found. Yet such heuristic searches can fail in two distinct ways: they offer no guarantee of returning a nearly optimal solution, and they obscure whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. Indeed, we show that standard scaling law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect (Breiman, 2001): the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. We resolve these issues with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorit

translated_title: 模糊的拟合：罗生门效应与缩放定律估计中的挑战
translated_abstract: 估计神经缩放定律涉及一个端到端的流程：设计缩放方案、跨尺度训练模型、在目标指标上评估模型，以及部署一种算法将缩放定律拟合到所得数据上。这最后的拟合阶段通常被视为常规操作：标准流程使用从初始点网格出发的局部优化来最小化一个非凸拟合损失，并返回找到的最优解。然而，这种启发式搜索可能以两种截然不同的方式失败：它们无法保证返回近似最优的解，并且掩盖了本质上不同的参数选择是否能够几乎同样好地拟合数据。事实上，我们证明了标准的缩放定律拟合存在罗生门效应（Breiman, 2001）：近最小化器的次水平集对应于宽广的参数区域，这些区域在大尺度上的外推结果会出现实质性分歧。我们通过一种确定性的分支定界算法来解决这些问题。
tldr: 本文揭示了神经缩放定律拟合中存在“罗生门效应”——多个本质不同的参数选择都能几乎同样好地拟合数据，但其外推结果在大尺度上差异巨大，并提出确定性分支定界算法来解决这一模糊性问题。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a Rashomon effect in neural scaling law fitting, where fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly equally well yet produce substantially divergent extrapolations at scale, and proposes a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm to resolve this ambiguity.
